limitations: Lack of randomization in the sequence of exposures (Paper 2, 4)
Gender differences not tested due to low statistical power/sample size (Paper 2, 4)
Subjects experienced fatigue throughout the long experiment (Paper 2)
Subjects may have influenced each other during voting (Paper 2)
Actual position of the subjects in the conceptual physiological zones was not measured (Paper 2)
Relatively low number of subjects (n=20 for feet and n=46 for hands in Paper 3, n=35 in Paper 4) might limit the ability to generalize findings to the population at large.
Differences in duration and total area of contact warming between the hand and the feet may have complicated findings (Paper 3)
Exposure sequencing effects were not addressed in Paper 3
Logistic regression models developed in Paper 3 may not be robust because they have not been validated with any other data.
